newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key points of U.S.-Japan insurance deal.
newsitem.headline: Key points of U.S.-Japan insurance deal.

text.p: While the details were still being discussed, the following are the basic agreements reached in the insurance talks between the United States and Japan, according to Japanese officials:

-- Non-life insurance subsidiaries of Japanese life insurance companies will be allowed to begin selling accident policies in January, part of the so-called specialty "third sector". They will not be allowed to offer travel insurance, however.
-- Japan's non-life sector, which includes auto and fire insurance, will be deregulated, including the freedom to set rates, by the end of 1998.
-- The third sector, in which foreign firms have a foothold, will be protected against any "radical changes" for 2-1/2 years after the deregulation of the non-life sector.
-- In 2001, the third sector areas of cancer and medical insurance will be opened to the Japanese non-life subsidiaries.

Japan and the United States reached agreement on Saturday on how Japan should open its insurance industry to foreign competitors, an esoteric row that grew into a major political issue between the two nations.
The dispute centred on U.S. charges that Japan planned to renege on a 1994 trade agreement on the deregulation of its $400 billion insurance market. tm/sposato
